7768901849823370877:
Mohist Hill distinguishes between its inner and outer gates. Entering the inner gate means delving into the abyss to seek pearls, planning for millennia; joining the outer gate focuses on refining tools for the benefit of all. 
Common folk say, "Is the division based on talent? The inner gate for the gifted, the outer gate for the lesser." But I think otherwise. 
During the Zhou Guangshun era, there was an outer gate disciple surnamed Mo. He challenged several Elders with his mechanical contraptions, winning three consecutive matches undefeated, leaving all in awe. 
His mechanisms prioritized function over form, crude in design, initially scorned by the inner gate. Yet after this battle, his fame soared, and the rugged style became a fleeting trend, with disciples proudly flaunting their rough-hewn devices. 
Nowadays, those Faded Memories have dimmed, but this trend alone endures.
